evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: "Just need to ask you some questions about it that might take about ten to fifteen minutes. Is that okay?" — time-boxed but no explicit promise of a dependable quote, and no clear wait for confirmation before moving forward.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: "Do you have any important concerns or instructions do that you want us to discuss on this call as well?" — asked early, before logistics probing started.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer: "if you guys can pack everything in my current department, move it and then unpack it on my new apartment." Rep: "Okay. So we can definitely help you with the packing and the moving portion. But we do not unpack the boxes..." — one response, no follow-up like 'tell me more about why unpacking is important to you' or similar.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Not present. No summary like 'So what I'm hearing is you want packing, moving, and unpacking — is that right?' offered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: "So, currently, I'm just estimating your move to take about six to eight hours which is an estimated budget of $1,821 including the packing supplies estimate." — typical range given ($102/hr × 2 movers, 6–8 hrs, plus $189 supplies estimate). Also personalized: accounts for walking distance and packing time.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: "If you need help with this assembly reassembly. Taxes, insurance, credit card fees. Basically everything is already in that price... no hidden fees of any type, no credit card fees, no transportation fees... two and a half hour minimum. If we go over, we only charge in fifteen minute intervals." — fee transparency and 2.5-hour minimum + 15-minute increment framing both present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: No recognizable 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent asked. Rep moves directly to the ask without testing customer reaction to the price.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: "on time, guarantee if we run late on the time we schedule, we provide discounts for your move" — delivered but terms are vague (what discount, how immediate?). Partial credit for mention without full clarity on discount start.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: "we will also include other features, like our no worries damage coverage. Which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair, replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages" — amount and purpose covered, but missing 'no deductible / no fine print' framing and no explicit 'built into the rate' language. Partial.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar closure after presenting the Two Promises.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: "So with that Christina, would you like our help for this move on the seventh?" — asked plainly, but customer deflects with 'Could you send me the estimate? And then I can confirm whenever I'm able to.' Rep then says 'if you're ready to go ahead with the booking just let us know' — softens into an out (email follow-up). Does not re-ask or hold for a commitment.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Email, date (7th October), and current/new addresses confirmed. Missing: phone number, arrival window, crew size, and notes left about concerns. Partial.

top_strength: Joanna gathered logistics details systematically and thoroughly — property type, floor, furniture specifics, fragile items, box count estimates, and walking distances — giving her solid material for an accurate quote.
coaching_note: Skip the 'send an email and they'll confirm later' close — ask plainly, wait for a yes-or-no answer, and if they hesitate, find the real objection rather than offering an out; also add a genuine final-concerns check before the ask instead of moving straight from pricing to the ask.
